sarah_cust: Hey team — seeing 403s from prod when calling /v1/generate starting ~09:12 UTC. Embeddings and rerank calls work fine. Example curl we use:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b", "prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response body: {"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"missing scope: generate"} — any quick suggestions? This is customer-facing so high priority.

jess_support: Thanks — can you paste the last 6 of the key id and confirm if this key was created via SSO/Okta provisioning or created manually in Console? Also which region/route you hit (us-east / eu-west)?

sarah_cust: last6 = 9af3d2, created by our SSO service account (Okta SCIM). We hit api.redwood.ai (us-east). Embeddings endpoint /v1/embeddings with same header works: returns 200. Rerank also returns 200. Only /v1/generate returns 403.

jess_support: copying infra/iam — sounds like token scopes might be incomplete. Can you confirm the exact error from our gateway logs (paste the full JSON you got)? The short message you sent shows missing generate scope.

sarah_cust: full error from client: {"status":403,"code":"insufficient_scope","detail":"token scopes: [embeddings,rerank], required: generate"}

deploy-bot: deploy completed: scim-provisioner v1.3.2 by @matt_infra — roll 2026-03-15T08:50:12Z :white_check_mark:

matt_infra: I see the deploy, digging in. Quick note: we shipped a small change to the SCIM mapping yesterday to split "inference" into "generate" and "stream_generate" for more granular perms. Looks like the default rule for SSO service accounts didn't get the new "generate" mapping, only assigned embeddings + rerank.

jess_support: ok — so this is a provisioning ruleset bug. Workaround options for the customer: 1) rotate/create a new API key via Console (manual flow sets full default scopes), 2) have an admin run the admin-key-create API to add the missing scope, or 3) we can fix the SCIM mapping and reprovision. Which do they prefer?

sarah_cust: customer wants fastest path — they can rotate keys. Any exact CLI/Console steps we can give them?

matt_infra: workaround curl to create a scoped key via our public console API (admin only):
```
# admin only, returns new key value
POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/admin/keys
Headers: Authorization: Bearer admin-replace-me
Body: {"name":"sso-service-rotated", "scopes": ["generate", "embeddings", "rerank"] }
```
If they don't have admin access, they can use Console UI: Console > Settings > API keys > Create key > check "generate" + others.

alex_iam: Filed RJ-2456 to update SCIM mappings and add an automatic validation that warns if newly provisioned keys lack any expected inference scopes. PR linked in ticket. Also scheduled rollback window if we need it.

sarah_cust: ok I asked their admin to create a new key via Console and they did that ~5m ago. They pasted the new key (redacted) and I tested — /v1/generate now returns 200 and tokens are producing text. :tada:

jess_support: awesome — can you confirm the new key last6 so we can mark the old key revoked and close out?
sarah_cust: new key last6 = b4c9e1, old key revoked. Customer confirmed full functionality restored.

iam-bot: noticed SCIM mapping change in recent deploy; created alert RJ-2456 (priority: high).

jess_support: Action items captured: (1) matt_infra/iam to revert or patch SCIM mapping in prod (RJ-2456), (2) add admin-facing validation that flags SSO-provisioned keys missing inference/generation scopes, (3) update runbook KB article: "SSO provisioning -> missing generate scope" with troubleshooting steps and Console workaround.

matt_infra: I'll push a hotfix to ensure default mapping includes "generate" and schedule a migration for existing service accounts. ETA 2 hours.

sarah_cust: thanks everybody — customer happy. Please keep me posted when fix is deployed. :heart:

jess_support: closing thread once RJ-2456 has PR merged and migration run. Adding notes to the customer ticket and KB.

(threads like this are often caused by changed scope names after a deploy — flagging for the release checklist to include a provisioning mapping smoke-test.)
